inventory_note: GPT uses these three auxiliary services plus one GEMM. Add, ReLU, GCN and SAD are excluded from this workload-specific projection. The installed-seven-core scenario is archived separately.
topology: Three local ASIC cores share a 128 KiB SPM and one upstream command endpoint; GEMM is the other endpoint. Four compute IPs do not mean four independent AutoLink endpoints.

area_model.equation: new cluster = old endpoint - five old units + three selected cores + (3/5 - 1)*(old shared memory peripheral + local controller + endpoint shell)

latency_model.equation: All old ASIC mode cycles multiply by P1 1-CGRA resident segment cycles / old small-case CGRA chain cycles; graph applies P1 1-CGRA graph/resident-segment ratio.

assumptions: Old operator and local-chain modes are proxies, not measurements of specialized task/segment hardware.
A single proportional workload scaling factor preserves old relative ASIC mode costs; attention, memory and control scaling can differ in reality.
Removing unused cores adds no latency relative to the old proxy; cluster scheduling, shared-SPM arbitration and buffering are not revalidated.
The existing linear peripheral/control model is extrapolated from five to three cores; SRAM payload remains 128 KiB. No redesigned cluster synthesis exists.
The three selected core areas include their synthesized native/local/configuration logic and local storage; old unit areas are removed to avoid double counting.
Existing P1 GEMM and shared-control costs are reused; new ownership/refill logic and achieved common clock are unverified.
CGRA values use the conservative minimum AE endpoint already selected for the main figure. The prior 75% refill-overlap scenario is archived separately and is not used in this table.

GPT single-CGRA data SRAM is projected at 32 KiB using the multicore compact-layout equations; address relocation and cycle invariance are not validated. Its peripheral logic is not re-synthesized. The ASIC cluster retains its original shared 128 KiB SPM.
